judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports independently uncovered the prior Edgerunner attempt/revert via git history and satisfied all four expectations with comparable specificity and quoted commit evidence; the two are essentially on par in depth and rigor.

report_1.evidence: The steps are unusually concrete because the repository contains a completed prior attempt (commits `454a21f`, `597777b`, `1712565`, ticket PLAT-31).

report_2.evidence: `git log --all --oneline` in `carelog-api` reveals that this exact migration was already done and reverted: `454a21f` "Add Edgerunner serverless deploy for API (PLAT-31)" (2026-04-14), `597777b` "Open a dedicated Postgres connection per request in the serverless handler (PLAT-31)" (2026-04-16), and `1712565` "Revert Edgerunner migration… /reports/monthly exhausted Postgres max_connections in production" (2026-04-21).

report_1.evidence: Commit `454a21f` (Apr 14, 2026) added the Edgerunner deploy; `597777b` (Apr 16) discovered isolates can't hold the SQLAlchemy pool and fell back to per-request connections; `1712565` (Apr 21) reverted everything, recording: "the per-request connections opened faster than Postgres could recycle them and tripped the connection limit ('FATAL: too many connections'), taking the endpoint down."

report_2.evidence: Commit `1712565` (2026-04-21) reverts the Edgerunner deployment because "serverless isolates cannot hold the Postgres pool" and per-request connections "opened faster than Postgres could recycle them and tripped the connection limit ('FATAL: too many connections'), taking the endpoint down" under *normal* dashboard load.

report_1.evidence: The migration already failed in production and was deliberately reverted, ~12 weeks ago. Commit `454a21f` (Apr 14, 2026) added the Edgerunner deploy; ... `1712565` (Apr 21) reverted everything ... keep the Cargobox deployment (`deploy/cargobox.yaml`) live until sustained clean operation, and only then decommission it.

report_2.evidence: the only commits since the revert are a dependency bump (`1b834c5`) and a test tidy (`e004559`). Re-running the same migration would reproduce the same outage. ... Run Edgerunner alongside the existing Cargobox service (leave `deploy/cargobox.yaml` and the `Dockerfile` in place)

report_1.evidence: The first deliverable should be presenting the PLAT-31 history (commits `454a21f` → `597777b` → `1712565`, April 14–21, 2026) to leadership, because the proposal re-opens a decision that was settled by a production outage less than three months ago... Who should be involved: the engineer/team who owned PLAT-31 and authored the revert (they hold context the commits don't capture)

report_2.evidence: The first action should be to surface commit `1712565` and the PLAT-31 ticket to leadership, since the cost-cutting premise has already been production-tested and the outage cost should be part of the calculus. ... People to involve: whoever owns PLAT-31 and authored the April revert (the platform team, per the PLAT scheme in `carelog-api/README.md`) — they hold the incident context
